doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Dialysis and being therapeutic through music
summary: Powell describes being a dialysis patient, treating it as his nine to five, and music as therapy.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: One person said if you do something that you love, you technically never have to work another day in your life, ‘cause it’s a love affair.

Yeah. Right. I don’t, just like dialysis for me. I’ve never had a nine to five in my life. When my kidneys broke down, and I had to start dialysis that was maybe about three or four years ago, no it must have been maybe a little before that. At any rate, what I did, I go to the hospital three times a week, three and a half hours. I made this my nine to five. And there are days when I feel like I don’t want to go and stuff. This is like, you realize you’ve got to go to work, I realize I’ve got to do this, so it doesn’t even interfere with my life. I go and do that, and in fact I do it all over the world. I was dialyzed in East Germany. It’s become an adventure. So, but the main thing is, be happy.
